title: Conduct, Culture and Behavioural Supervision
summary: An eight-module programme on assessing conduct risk and culture in firms, using behavioural insights, data and targeted supervisory interventions.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors to assess conduct risk and culture in regulated firms, using behavioural insights, data and targeted interventions to identify the drivers of poor customer outcomes and misconduct.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical grounding in how consumer behaviour, firm culture and incentives drive conduct outcomes, and how to supervise them. Participants leave able to assess culture and the governance of conduct, challenge product governance and sales practices, use behavioural and data tools, and choose effective supervisory interventions.
sections.What It Covers: Behavioural economics in consumer markets, assessing culture and the governance of conduct, incentives and remuneration, product governance and fair value, sales practices and distribution, data and behavioural supervision tools, misconduct and individual accountability, and supervisory interventions.
Intended Audience: Conduct and consumer protection supervisors, including those supervising retail-facing firms
Prudential and governance supervisors seeking to assess culture and its link to risk
Policy, data and enforcement staff working on conduct risk and customer outcomes
Learning Objectives: Explain how behavioural biases in consumers and firms shape conduct outcomes
Assess a firm's culture and the governance and accountability arrangements for conduct
Evaluate incentives, product governance and sales practices for conduct risk
Apply data and behavioural tools to identify poor outcomes and emerging harm
Identify indicators of misconduct and test individual accountability
Select and design proportionate supervisory interventions that change behaviour
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, file and journey reviews and a supervisory question set, and can be selected or tailored to the authority's conduct priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of conduct or consumer protection supervision is helpful. No background in economics or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)

modules.title: Behavioural Economics in Consumer Markets
modules.summary: How consumers actually make financial decisions, the biases firms can exploit or mitigate, and why behavioural insights change how supervisors define and detect conduct risk.
objectives: Explain the main behavioural biases affecting consumer financial decisions
Identify how product design and presentation can exploit those biases
Assess the implications of behavioural insights for conduct supervision
syllabus: Limited attention, present bias, inertia and overconfidence
Choice architecture, defaults, framing and sludge
Where behavioural harm arises: complex products, pricing and add-ons
From disclosure-based to outcomes-focused supervision

modules.title: Assessing Culture and the Governance of Conduct
modules.summary: How supervisors assess firm culture through its drivers and observable behaviours, and how boards and senior managers govern conduct risk and are held accountable for it.
objectives: Explain the drivers of culture and why supervisors assess them
Assess board oversight, management information and accountability for conduct
Gather and triangulate evidence on culture from multiple sources
syllabus: Drivers of culture: purpose, leadership, people, governance and incentives
Board oversight of conduct and senior manager accountability regimes
Evidence of culture: interviews, focus groups, surveys and documents
Red flags: tone at the top versus behaviour in the middle

modules.title: Incentives, Remuneration and Performance Management
modules.summary: How sales targets, remuneration and performance management shape behaviour, and how supervisors assess whether incentive schemes encourage poor outcomes or misconduct.
objectives: Explain how incentives drive front-line and management behaviour
Evaluate the design and controls of incentive and remuneration schemes
Identify incentive structures linked to poor outcomes and mis-selling
syllabus: Variable pay, sales targets and balanced scorecards
Non-financial incentives: promotion, recognition and pressure
Controls: deferral, malus, clawback and quality gateways
Case studies: incentive-driven mis-selling

modules.title: Product Governance and Fair Value
modules.summary: How to assess firms' product design, target market definition, testing, fair value assessments and post-sale review across the product lifecycle.
objectives: Assess product approval, target market and distribution strategy
Apply a fair value framework to a financial product
Evaluate post-sale monitoring and product review
syllabus: The product lifecycle: design, approval, distribution and review
Target market definition and consumer testing
Fair value: price, quality, cross-subsidy and outcomes
Post-sale monitoring and product withdrawal or remediation

modules.title: Sales Practices and Distribution
modules.summary: How products reach consumers through advice, non-advised, digital and intermediary channels, and how supervisors identify pressure selling, mis-selling and poor treatment of vulnerable customers.
objectives: Identify conduct risks across advised, non-advised and digital channels
Assess sales processes, scripts and digital journeys for harmful practices
Evaluate the treatment of vulnerable customers in sales and servicing
syllabus: Distribution models and the role of intermediaries
Pressure selling, bundling, cross-selling and dark patterns
Mystery shopping and testing digital customer journeys
Vulnerable customers in sales and servicing

modules.title: Data and Behavioural Supervision Tools
modules.summary: How supervisors use firm data, complaints, market intelligence and behavioural methods to detect poor outcomes early and target supervisory attention.
objectives: Identify data sources that indicate poor customer outcomes
Apply analytical and behavioural tools to detect emerging harm
Assess firms' own conduct management information and outcome testing
syllabus: Outcome indicators: complaints, cancellations, persistency and arrears
Market intelligence, whistleblowing and consumer research
Behavioural methods: experiments, surveys and journey analysis
Testing firms' conduct dashboards and outcome monitoring

modules.title: Misconduct, Speaking Up and Individual Accountability
modules.summary: How misconduct arises and spreads, how firms detect and respond to it, and how supervisors test speak-up arrangements, conduct rules and the accountability of individuals.
objectives: Explain how misconduct arises, normalises and spreads within firms
Assess speak-up, whistleblowing and conduct breach arrangements
Evaluate how firms hold individuals to account for misconduct
syllabus: Rationalisation, normalisation and the bystander effect
Speak-up and whistleblowing arrangements and their effectiveness
Conduct breaches, disciplinary action and references
Linking misconduct findings to fitness and propriety

modules.title: Supervisory Interventions and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining the interventions that change firm behaviour, from dialogue and thematic work to redress and enforcement referral, applied in an integrated case study.
objectives: Select interventions proportionate to the conduct and culture issues identified
Design interventions that address root causes rather than symptoms
Evaluate whether interventions have changed behaviour and outcomes
syllabus: The intervention toolkit: dialogue, thematic reviews, remediation and redress
Using behavioural insights to design supervisory communications
Measuring the impact of supervisory interventions
Workshop: a culture and conduct case study and intervention plan

related.title: Consumer Protection and Financial Inclusion
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess product governance, fair value, disclosure, vulnerable customer treatment, complaints and financial inclusion.

related.title: Cross-Border and Group Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module programme on home-host supervision, consolidated group oversight, MoUs, supervisory colleges, third-country firms and cross-border crisis cooperation.

related.title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.
